description: 2 tactical challenges for Black against the Légal Trap. Decline the poisoned queen and keep the extra bishop pair.

drills.briefExplanation: 5...Bxf3! 6.Qxf3 Nf6 — trade the bishop before White can set the trap.
drills.description: Black to play. White kicked the bishop with 5.h3 — don't retreat into the trap.
drills.explanation: The safe way to meet 5.h3: 5...Bxf3! trades the bishop before White's trap is set. After 6.Qxf3 Nf6 Black has the bishop pair and a solid Philidor structure — White's h3 is a slight weakening, and there are no tactics to fear. Sometimes the best defense is refusing to play the opponent's game.
drills.name: Trading Before the Trap

drills.briefExplanation: 6...dxe5! 7.Qxh5 Nf6 — take back with the pawn and let White's 'trap' win nothing.
drills.description: Black to play. White offered the queen with 6.Nxe5 — decline it correctly.
drills.explanation: The critical defensive resource: 6...dxe5! simply takes back with the pawn. After 7.Qxh5 Nf6 White has won the bishop pair but Black is completely solid — the e5 pawn controls the center, the knight develops with tempo, and the 'trap' has netted White nothing. Greed (6...Bxd1??) gets mated; calm recapture gets equality.
drills.name: Declining the Queen
